applies_why: The judge text decides the link by saying paternity lacks explicit textual resolution, which invokes a stating-verse-style requirement rather than chain-by-footing weighing.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires' read either as barring a demand for an explicit contrary/resolving verse or as still allowing that lack of explicit textual resolution leaves a chain underdetermined; I apply the first reading because the rule expressly retires the stating-verse test.
why: By marking the issue underdetermined for lack of 'explicit textual resolution of paternity,' the judge applies the retired stating-verse test instead of weighing the chains by footing.
